reasons: Classification is correct: Section 14.5 contains only a mutual consequential-damages waiver and carve-outs, with no aggregate monetary cap, so it fails the fallback's material term (mutual cap of 12 months' fees) — a genuine deviation rather than an acceptable fallback clause.

The redline is directionally right and additive: it preserves the existing waiver and the existing carve-out sentence and inserts a single mutual cap sentence at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid/payable by Sanofi and USD 1,000,000, plus an 'Excluded Claims' definition capturing indemnification (14.1/14.2), confidentiality (Art. XI), IP (Art. X), gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, and confirming payment obligations are not 'damages' — matching the model language and redline guidance.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is advisory only; the high changed-character ratio reflects the necessary insertion of a cap sentence into a short clause, not a rewrite — the original sentences remain intact and no contradictory language is created (the retained 'notwithstanding' sentence is consistent with the new carve-outs, if mildly redundant).

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the playbook position and that indemnities/confidentiality/IP sit outside the cap; the cap is mutual so it does not create one-sided exposure for Customer.

Minor, non-blocking: the inserted carve-out list omits explicit data protection/security obligations (only partially covered via Art. XI), which is a sub-element short of preferred wording and could be noted rather than redlined further.
